summary_1line: Vidura advises Dhritarashtra on wisdom, friendship, secrecy, virtue, and ruling justly—warning him to restrain Duryodhana and reconcile with the Pandavas.

image_candidates.scene_text: Vidura stands before the blind king Dhritarashtra in the royal court, speaking stern wisdom while courtiers listen in tense silence.
A guilty man lies awake at night in a dark chamber, staring at a snake coiled beside him on the floor.
A fragile stone raft sinks in water while people cling to it, symbolizing foolish leaders guiding others to ruin.
